title: Tutor mode

body.text: Claude is a good tutor when you tell it to
teach Socratically: ask leading questions, hint step by step, don't reveal the answer right away
— figuring it out yourself is what makes it stick, unlike copying the answer.

example: "Be my grade-11 physics tutor: I'll send a problem — don't give the answer directly, ask leading questions step by step until I find it myself"

title: Adapt the teaching to the learner

body.text: Tell it your level and the style you learn best with:
— and ask for more practice on the points you still get wrong; the AI will tune the difficulty to fit you.

example: "I get supply-demand now, but I'm still confused about elasticity — re-explain with a bubble-tea-shop example, then give me 3 practice problems"

options.text: Leading questions to make you think, without revealing the answer right away
Giving away every answer as fast as possible

question: Why is figuring it out yourself better than copying the answer?

options.text: It makes you actually remember and understand
It's just slower, with no upside

question: What should you tell the AI so it teaches at the right level?

options.text: Your knowledge level and the kind of examples you find easy

question: To get Claude to teach at your level, what should you do?

options.text: Always have it teach at the hardest level
State your background and have it adapt to your understanding

question: What's the benefit of adapting the teaching to the learner?

options.text: Easier to understand and you don't get lost
